notes.q01: Code -1 (low). The NDP government repealed the consumer carbon tax and the Minister of Finance defended the consequences in Hansard on 2026-02-18 ('when the carbon tax was removed, so too did we remove that'), with the rationale that the tax 'did not land evenly'. A party that repealed the tax is on record against reinstating it, so code negative; -1 not -2 because the quote is a budget explanation of the homeowner-grant cut rather than an explicit pledge against reinstatement. Mapping required judgment (Hansard inference).
notes.q03: Code null (n/a). Null: no fetched NDP source states a position on a wealth tax on large personal fortunes. The wealth-tax passages in ndp-0024/ndp-0025 are BC Green MLAs (Botterell, Valeriote) proposing it to the government; per CODEBOOK §5 an opponent's characterization of the government's refusal is not evidence of the NDP's position. The party's 2026 platform rhetoric ('instead of giving tax breaks to the top 2%') is about income-tax breaks, not a wealth tax instrument.
notes.q04: Code -1 (medium). Government member Steve Morissette speaking for Budget 2026 (Hansard 2026-02-19): the party's goal is deficit reduction WITHOUT cutting services ('Let me state plainly that this is not an austerity budget'). The statement's instrument (balance the budget by cutting spending) is rejected; the balance goal itself is only partially shared (reduce, not balance) -> tie-breaker yields -1, not -2. Right position on a related instrument = medium.
notes.q10: Code 1 (medium). BC NDP 'Action for You' policy page (published 2024-01-04, predates the 2026 campaign): the party records having 'removed barriers' (provincial rule/zoning changes, cf. adjacent sentence 'We've fixed restrictive and outdated rules that were blocking townhouses, row homes and duplexes') to deliver more homes near transit hubs. Same instrument (provincial override of local rules for housing near transit) but a weaker/more permissive instrument than the statement's 'require' -> +1. Document date 2024-01-04 per CODEBOOK §4 -> medium at most.
